subject: SIG: Access controls evidence — tenant mapping & SCIM push issues
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@acmecloud.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jennifer Lee <jennifer@okta-partner.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up — SCIM sync tenant mapping behavior

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for answering the initial SIG sections. We're doing a final pass on access controls and hit a small implementation question that came up during our internal review: when we provision users into Redwood from our IdP via SCIM, we see two identities created for certain contractors — one under our main tenant and a second under a legacy sub-tenant. Our security team needs a short explanation of why SCIM sometimes creates duplicate entries and whether Redwood can prevent cross-tenant provisioning by default.

Specifically, can you confirm: 
- whether SCIM push enforces tenant scoped provisioning (attribute-based) or relies on customer-side filtering,
- what default RBAC mapping happens when an incoming SCIM user has no group membership, and
- whether MFA enforcement is applied at provisioning or only at first sign-in.

If you can point us to the SCIM attribute map and any recommended config to avoid the duplicate-tenant issue, that would help close our SIG evidence.

Thanks,
Samir
Customer Security — Acme Cloud

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jennifer Lee <jennifer@okta-partner.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — SCIM sync tenant mapping behavior

Hi Samir — quick reply while I pull the attachments together. Short answers:
- SCIM is configured to include a tenant attribute (tenant_id) in the push by default for our integrations. If your IdP is sending a legacy attribute (e.g., org) we accept it, which can create a separate identity if the attribute maps to a different tenant namespace.
- If no groups are present, users land in the customer-defined default role ("user") — we do not elevate privileges automatically.
- MFA policy enforcement is evaluated at authentication time; provisioning does not register MFA but can mark an account as "mfa_required" which trips enforcement on first login.

I'll attach the scim_attribute_map.csv and an updated SIG answers PDF. Jennifer — can you confirm if Okta has any filtering rules that would rewrite the tenant attribute on push?

Best,
Priyom
Manager, Security & Compliance

Priyom — forwarding my triage notes so we have a consistent reply to Acme. See my short checklist below (I'll include these in the final SIG response):

- Confirmed default attribute: "tenant_id" (string) is canonical; we also accept "organization" for backwards compatibility but prefer customers map to "tenant_id".
- Recommended Okta filter: add a transform rule to map acme_org -> tenant_id to prevent legacy org values being pushed.
- RBAC default: default role = user; no admin rights unless group maps to one of the admin roles.
- Edge case: contractor accounts created via CSV bulk create do not set tenant_id unless CSV includes column; add post-provisioning script to backfill.

I'll prepare a one-paragraph explanation for the SIG PDF to make it explicit why duplicates occur and the steps to avoid it. Also captured the small troubleshooting repro steps from Acme and attached the screenshot they sent.

Hi Samir — following up with the final wording we plan to include in the SIG evidence pack and a recommended config for your Okta tenant. Key points below — feel free to paste into your auditor notes: 

1) Root cause & behavior (2 lines): When a SCIM push includes an attribute that resolves to a different tenant namespace (e.g., legacy org or alternate tenant_id), Redwood creates the identity under that namespace to preserve source-of-truth fidelity. This can look like a duplicate account when multiple values exist in your IdP.

2) Mitigation (recommended config): Configure an Okta transform rule to map your authoritative attribute to "tenant_id" on push, and add a filter to drop legacy org values. Example transform: if user.profile.org exists then user.profile.tenant_id = user.profile.org; else tenant_id = <default>.

3) RBAC & least privilege: Users provisioned with no groups receive the default role "user". Admin roles require explicit group mapping; we never autoassign elevated roles on provisioning.

4) MFA handling: Provisioning sets account metadata (mfa_required flag) but MFA challenge is enforced at first authentication against your configured IdP policies. For high-risk contractor flows we recommend enabling conditional access policies on the IdP to require MFA for unknown devices.

I've attached the CSV mapping and the updated SIG PDF to this thread. Dev — can you add a one-line note in the SIG PDF about the post-provisioning backfill script we run for CSV imports? I'll upload the final package to the shared Drive link.

Thanks — will keep the HubSpot record updated (HubSpot-ACME-2345) when you confirm the transform.

Best,
